entities.name: Sima Qian
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Chinese historian (c. 145–86 BCE) and author of the Shiji (Records of the Grand Historian), considered the father of Chinese historiography and one of the greatest historians in world history. Born into a family of court historiographers, Sima Qian traveled widely across China collecting oral traditions and documentary sources before succeeding his father as Grand Historian (Taishi) at the Han court. When he defended the disgraced general Li Ling, Emperor Wu sentenced him to castration — the most humiliating punishment for a man in ancient China. Rather than commit suicide (the honorable alternative), Sima Qian chose to live and complete his father's vision, writing in a famous letter: "I swallowed my grief and bore my shame, for I had not yet completed my book." The result was a work of staggering scope, literary power, and historical honesty that defined Chinese historical writing forever.
